_note: FIVE DESTINATIONS, and the board names them in its own title: stock
browser · icon picker · versions · used-in · image editor. They are joined
SEPARATELY below, and the two that are not joined are named with the reason,
not folded into the others.
REACHED VIA PROBE: four of the five mount side by side, each in the
positioned drawer-width host they are `absolute inset-0` inside — mounting
one bare stretches it to the probe root and every width reads wrong. These
are the shipping overlays; nothing is re-implemented.
BOARD WON, five times:
75:65   the CURRENT version is a 44-high accent-tint chip on a 6 radius at
a 10 inset — the same box the older rows wear in bg-subtle. It
shipped 56 tall, full-bleed and square.
75:90   the used-in list is one CHIP PER HIT — page name over the
element's own name, with a 'Go ›' link — and NO page-group header.
It shipped a 28-high bg-subtle header per page over bare rows,
which put the page name in two places and left the row with no
shape at all. Flattening it also removed three contrast failures
(the headers' own ink-muted-on-bg-subtle).
75:100  the link says 'Go ›'. It said 'Jump ›'.
75:25   the icon picker is SIX up on a 12 gutter, and its tiles fill their
track rather than floating a fixed 40 square in the middle of one.
It shipped five up at a 16 gutter — and IconBrowserOverlay's own
docstring has said '6-up grid' the whole time, so the markup was
the half that drifted.
75:6    the stock results are THREE up on a 12 gutter with an 8 gap and a
66-tall thumb. It shipped two up at a 16 gutter with 76-tall
thumbs — two big cards where the board draws a contact sheet.
NOT JOINED, and why:
75:15/16 (stock thumbs) and 75:34/35 (icon tiles) — every one carries a
track width derived from a 320 drawer (93.333 and 42.667). The drawer is
280 today; PageCommandPalette's own comment records the same supersession
('256 is the drawer's 280 less a 12 gutter … the 296 this carried was the
same arithmetic against the old 320 drawer'). Their fill, height and
radius ARE conformed and are in `measured/`; hosting the probe at 320 to
make the number match would be measuring a width no user has.
75:101 (the 'Menu' used-in chip) — the board gives THAT one row a raw
`rounded-[8px]` while its two siblings use --radius/md (6). Board noise:
one row of three. The other two are joined and the code follows the token.
75:113 THE IMAGE EDITOR, the fifth destination — a 1000-wide full-bleed
takeover: a 48-high bg-subtle bar, four 28-high outlined tools (Crop /
Rotate / Adjust / Replace) on --color/border-input, an accent 'Save as v5',
and an ink stage. That is ImageEditorModal, a separate component reached
through `onEditImage`, and it is a build rather than a restyle. Its
numbers are recorded here so whoever takes it does not have to re-read the
board.
CONTRAST, REPORTED NOT HIDDEN — three failures at 4.39:1 that conforming
PRODUCED, and they are the board's own pairing: 75:99 puts the element's
name in --color/ink-muted #6B7280 on 75:96's --color/bg-subtle #F3F4F6
ground, which measures 4.39 against a 4.5 floor. The board draws it that
way; the code now does too. Net for this surface the count went DOWN (the
page-group headers this replaced carried the same pair three times over),
but it is not zero and should not be read as zero. The fix is one step
darker on the sub-line (--bk-ink-soft #4B5563 is 7.0 there), which is a
founder call because it deviates from the board. The fourth failure,
'current' on the accent-tint version chip, is pre-existing.
FOUND AND FIXED — a probe fixture that had been measuring nothing.
`USAGE_COMPOSER` answered only `elements.getAllPages`, but
`collectUsageByPage` calls `composer.mediaOps.getUsagesByPage`
(mediaUtils.ts:162). So the existing `media-detail-used-in` case had been
rendering the EMPTY state — 'Not used on any page' — for as long as it has
existed, and nothing noticed because no recipe measured it. The fixture now
answers the call the code makes.
FOUND, NOT FIXED: 75:111, a warning-tint 'delete guard' — 'Deleting this
breaks 3 pages. Replace it instead.' — sits under the used-in list on the
board. The product has the empty-state counterpart ('Deleting this file
won't change anything on your site') but nothing for the NON-empty case,
which is the one where deleting is dangerous. That is a missing block, not
drift.
